reason: The sources provide over 10 cross-validated claims from multiple independent websites detailing the Shapley Supercluster's discovery, mass, location, and gravitational pull on the Milky Way.
story: In 1930, astronomer Harlow Shapley spotted an extraordinary concentration of galaxies in the constellation Centaurus, 650 million light-years away. Decades later, scientists realized this structure—the Shapley Supercluster—was far more colossal than a simple cloud of galaxies. Packing over 8,000 galaxies with a total mass exceeding ten million billion Suns, it is the most massive structure within a billion light-years of Earth. For years, astronomers thought our Milky Way was being pulled primarily by a mysterious region known as the Great Attractor. However, deeper surveys revealed a staggering revelation: the Great Attractor itself, along with the Milky Way and our entire local region of space, is being dragged across the cosmos toward the overwhelming gravitational grip of the Shapley Supercluster.
angle: Our entire galaxy, along with the Great Attractor itself, is being pulled across space toward the Shapley Supercluster—a colossal titan holding over 8,000 galaxies and 10 million billion solar masses.

claims.claim: Harlow Shapley first discovered a striking concentration of galaxies in 1930.
The Shapley Supercluster is located in the constellation Centaurus.
The center of the Shapley Supercluster is situated approximately 650 million light-years from Earth.
The Shapley Supercluster contains more than 8,000 galaxies.
The supercluster has a total mass greater than ten million billion times the mass of the Sun.
It is the most massive cosmic structure within a distance of about one billion light-years from the Milky Way.
The Milky Way and our local region of galaxies are moving toward the Shapley Supercluster.
The Great Attractor itself is moving toward the Shapley Supercluster.
Somak Raychaudhury named the supercluster after Harlow Shapley in 1989.
Roberto Scaramella and co-workers identified the structure in 1989 and named it the Alpha concentration.
Abell 3558 is a major galaxy cluster located within the core of the Shapley Supercluster.
Abell 3562 is a galaxy cluster located inside the Shapley Supercluster.

disputed: Exact number of galaxy clusters in the Shapley Supercluster: S1 mentions 11 core clusters in one paper and 28 clusters in another, while S7 lists 25 major clusters. A script should leave out specific cluster totals or attribute 'containing dozens of major galaxy clusters'.

Primary cause of peculiar motion: Sources vary on whether the Great Attractor or the Shapley Supercluster is the primary driver, or if dipole repellers contribute. A script should frame it as an interconnected gravitational flow.
